stem: A 26-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral valve disease has had 3 weeks of low fever and tiredness that began after a root canal. A new apical holosystolic murmur is heard. Blood cultures grow Gram-positive cocci in chains that are alpha-hemolytic, resistant to optochin and insoluble in bile.
oneliner: 26F + rheumatic mitral valve + 3 wk low fever after root canal + new murmur + GPC in chains, alpha-hemolytic, optochin resistant, bile insoluble → which organism?
ask: Which organism is most likely responsible?

options.B: Viridans group streptococci (S. mitis, S. sanguinis)

whyNot.A: Also alpha-hemolytic, but **optochin sensitive and bile soluble**
whyNot.D: **Gamma-hemolytic, grows in bile and 6.5% salt**; after GI or urinary procedures

why: **Subacute endocarditis on a damaged valve after dental work + alpha-hemolytic, optochin-resistant, bile-insoluble streptococci** = viridans group. Their **dextran** helps them stick to fibrin-platelet clumps on the valve.

bug.name: Viridans streptococci (S. mitis, S. sanguinis, S. mutans)
bug.type: Gram-positive cocci in chains, catalase negative
bug.virulence: Dextran binds fibrin-platelet aggregates on damaged valves
bug.spread: Normal mouth flora; enters blood with dental work
bug.causes: Subacute endocarditis on abnormal valves; dental caries (S. mutans)
